title: AI slop movies are the new direct-to-video cash grabs
slides: AI slop movies flood streaming—but who actually profits?
Studios now generate full movies without human actors.
Yet these films earn more than low-budget indies do.
Gig economy writers face a new competitor: algorithms.
Watch one: check the credits for an AI studio name.
thread_text:
How did this happen?

One AI-generated film earned $12 million on streaming last year while its human-made budget was zero.

The math that broke Hollywood.

Studios now produce full-length movies using generative video tools, removing actors, sets, and camera crews.

Algorithms beat artistry.

These films consistently outearn low-budget indie movies, which often need a festival run just to break even.

Your favorite writer just got a new boss.

Gig economy screenwriters now compete with large language models that can script a plot in seconds.

Find one yourself.

Open Netflix, pick a random low-budget title, and scroll to the credits. If you see "Flawless AI" or "Runway," you found it.

instagram.caption:
Last year, one AI-generated film with zero human cast costs pulled in $12 million on streaming.

Studios are now cranking out full-length movies using generative video tools—no actors, no sets, no camera crews 📼 These films consistently out-earn indie projects that need a festival run just to break even. Meanwhile, freelance screenwriters suddenly face competition from algorithms that script a plot in seconds.

For anyone writing, filming, or editing for a living, your direct rival just went from “other creators” to “no one you can pitch to.”

Open Netflix tonight, pick a random low-budget title, and check the credits 🎬 You’ll either see “Flawless AI” or “Runway”—which one did you find first?
